_why_this_exists_before_the_review_does: AUT-PROP-006. This record is written as the seat's FIRST act, so a seat that dies leaves evidence that it looked rather than nothing at all. It is EMPTY and says so: publish_bar.clause_1_hardening_converged REFUSES any round with an open record at the commit it is grading, because an unfinished look must never be counted as a clean one.
central_claim: The published FET-fusion -> impaired-ATM -> compensatory-ATR-dependency mechanism, inherited by EMC as a CLASS claim and never tested on any NR4A3 fusion, has weak computational support in public data: EMC's structural precondition splits (type 2 MET; the commonest type 1 and type 5 NOT_MET), EMC tumours carry no proliferation-independent DDR transcriptional signature on two series (tier WEAK), the CRISPR dependency readout stays saturated even against a matched sarcoma comparator, and only 1 of 4 pre-registered drug-response mechanism tests passes - a module-level rather than ATR-specific internal-consistency check. No EMC-specific ATR vulnerability is reported and no efficacy claim is made.

blockers.summary: S2.1 misstates what the primary source behind the Cellosaurus caution says. The paper claims PMID 34413129 'names H-EMC-SS once, in a Materials-and-Methods cell-line list, and states no per-line fusion result', and that the caution is 'not a finding quoted from it'. A committed artifact quotes an explicit per-line fusion result from that paper's Figure 2A legend.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/hemcss-label-priorart.json -> papers_on_this_line.the_one_published_observation (pmid 34413129, pmcid PMC8571037, Gartrell 2021, Molecular cancer therapeutics) carries verbatim_quote: 'Although extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma (EMC) cancers such as H-EMC-SS typically have EWSR1-NR4A3 fusions, we did not detect a EWSR1 -translocation in this line.'; location: 'Figure 2A legend. Verified verbatim in the fetched full text (S9).'; significance: 'THIS IS THE NEAR-MISS AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR ANY NOVELTY CLAIM. The observation is in print. "Nobody has ever reported this" would be FALSE.' The same field states the narrower true caveat: what_it_is_not: 'no results sentence, figure, table or supplement reports the assay for this line; the "n >= 2" in that legend is the drug-assay replicate count; the methods' PCR/FISH sentence is a blanket statement over the whole panel naming no probe, no primer and no per-line result; and the paper does not state whether an EWSR1 break-apart FISH (which WOULD exclude EWSR1::NR4A3 whatever the partner) or an EWSR1-FLI1 RT-PCR (which would NOT) was performed.' So the naming is in a figure legend rather than only a Methods list, a per-line fusion result IS stated, and the Cellosaurus caution restates a published observation. As written the manuscript understates the evidence for its own 'most consequential finding' and would falsify any novelty framing built on it.
blockers.fix: Replace the sentence with the artifact's own distinction: PMID 34413129 states the result for this line in its Figure 2A legend ('we did not detect a EWSR1-translocation in this line'), so the Cellosaurus caution restates a published observation rather than issuing an unsourced curatorial verdict; what the paper does not report is the ASSAY - no results sentence, figure, table or supplement gives a per-line method, and it does not say whether an EWSR1 break-apart FISH (which would exclude EWSR1::NR4A3 with any partner) or an EWSR1-FLI1 RT-PCR (which would not) was used. Keep the conclusion that S2.2's boundary rests on the two DepMap readouts, now for the right reason: the published sentence has an unspecified assay.

blockers.summary: 'Two decades apart' is wrong by about a factor of four, and it is used twice as the argument for the strength of part B's two-series concordance - the paper's only positively-bounded finding.
blockers.evidence: Manuscript line 134 ('on two independent series two decades and two array technologies apart') and line 550 ('Two independent series, two decades apart, two array technologies... That concordance is what makes this a result rather than a single series' quirk'). research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature.series_seeds records both deposits verbatim: GSE4303 'GEO series title: "Gene expression profile of extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma." (36 samples, 2006/03/15)' and GSE24369 'GSM600934-GSM600939 titled "Extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma 1".."6" in the GEO DataSets index (42 samples, 2011/05/02)'. Five years and two months. It is also inconsistent with the manuscript's own S7 ('an annotation bridge for a 2005 array'; 'sitting in GEO since 2011').
blockers.fix: Both occurrences: 'five years and two array technologies apart', or drop the temporal claim and keep 'two array technologies, two comparator sets'. The platform and comparator independence, which is what carries the argument, is untouched.

blockers.summary: S8 attributes text to the Cancer Letters paper's abstract and tells the reader that abstract is quoted verbatim in the artifact. The artifact records that nothing beyond the search record was retrieved for that PMID, and holds no abstract for it.
blockers.evidence: Manuscript S8.1 publication row: 'not open access, so only the abstract was read and it is quoted verbatim in the artifact rather than paraphrased here'; S8.2 Q1: 'The paper's *abstract* states the authors pharmacotyped patient-derived cell models and tested ATRi/WEE1i/PARP1/2i combinations'. research/modalities/atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json -> associated_publication.candidate_publication_read['41651400'] = {'fulltext': 'CANNOT_DETERMINE - no open-access full text was retrievable; only the search record above was read', 'pmid': '41651400'}. All five occurrences of that PMID in the artifact were checked: the only stored fields are title, authors, journal, doi and year inside further_searches.*.hits. No abstract. The pharmacotyping / ATRi-WEE1i-PARP1/2i sentence IS in the artifact, but as series_record.summary - the GEO submitter summary - not as the journal abstract. This is the same one-of-a-pair provenance defect the Appendix already records twice for S8.
blockers.fix: Attribute the statement to the GEO series summary (atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json -> series_record.summary, quoted verbatim in the artifact) and say the journal abstract was not retrievable, in the artifact's own 'CANNOT_DETERMINE' terms. S8.2 Q1's bound ('an abstract is a claim by its authors, not a measurement read here') applies unchanged to a GEO summary and should stay.

blockers.summary: S3.4 mislabels the GSE24369 comparator arm: the six samples are myxofibrosarcoma, not fibrosarcoma. The label is a substring-matching artifact of the module's classifier, and the same document names the entity correctly in S8.
blockers.evidence: Manuscript S3.4 table: '29 - 17 LGFMS (FUS::CREB3L2...), 6 desmoid/fibromatosis, 6 fibrosarcoma'. research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature.per_platform['GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz'].sample_annotations_verbatim gives GSM600957-GSM600962 as 'Myxofibrosarcoma 1..6 | soft tissue | sample type: tumor biopsy | tissue: Myxofibrosarcoma'. The bucket name comes from research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 302, "'fibrosarcoma': ('fibrosarcoma',)" - a substring that 'Myxofibrosarcoma' contains, the same defect class S3.0 point 3 reports for the \\bemc\\b boundary. S8.1 of the same manuscript lists 'myxofibrosarcoma 14' as a distinct entity, so the two sections name one tumour type two ways.
blockers.fix: Print '6 myxofibrosarcoma' in the S3.4 table, and note that the classifier's 'fibrosarcoma' key matches myxofibrosarcoma by substring if the bucket is left as is. No verdict, group size or contrast changes.

p1s.summary: The FET-fusion status of the 17-sample LGFMS comparator arm is inherited from a disease label, with no per-sample fusion call and no citation anywhere in the repository - the exact inference the document forbids in three other places.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript S3.4 '17 LGFMS (FUS::CREB3L2, i.e. another FET fusion)' and S3.0 point 1 'its comparator arm is FUS::CREB3L2-rearranged, i.e. another FET fusion, which is the contrast this part most wants'. research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature.per_platform['GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz'].sample_annotations_verbatim carries no fusion field for GSM600940-GSM600956; every row reads 'Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma N | soft tissue | sample type: tumor biopsy | tissue: Low-grade fibromyxoid sarcoma'. The only basis in the repository is a code comment, research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 328 ('LGFMS added 2026-08-05: FUS::CREB3L2 is a FET fusion...'), with FET_COMPARATOR_BUCKETS on line 330. No PMID, in the manuscript or the module. Against this: S2 refuses the EMC label on ACH-001519 for want of a fusion call; S4 says 'FET status from DepMap's own filtered fusion calls, never from disease labels'; S8.3 says 'A label is not a fusion'. The claim is almost certainly true of LGFMS as a class, which is why this is a P1 rather than a blocker - but nothing reads it, and it is load-bearing for 'two different comparator sets - including one made of another FET fusion'.
p1s.fix: Cite the LGFMS/FUS::CREB3L2 frequency, and add the disclosure S4 already makes for its own arms: this arm's FET status is inherited from the disease label, not called per sample. atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json -> fet_fusion_sarcoma_subtypes._bound already carries the wording ('Presence of a DISEASE whose defining fusion is a FET fusion. It is not a per-sample fusion call') and can be reused.

p1s.summary: S7's provenance sentence is over-scoped: several numbers 'above' it come from three other producing modules and are not in emc-atr-vulnerability.json at all.
p1s.evidence: S7: 'Every number above is produced by emc_atr_vulnerability.py and lives in its JSON artifact; nothing is hand-typed here that the artifact does not carry, and --check re-derives all of it offline.' The headline's structural numbers (type 2 0 of 30, type 1 8 of 30, type 5 11 of 30, EWSR1::ATF1 fraction 0.267) live in emc-fet-idr-census.json -> positive_controls / emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3 and emc-fet-construct-designs.json -> constructs[*].domains_retained_and_lost; the headline's imported group difference (paclitaxel -0.5255 / t -3.076, azd6738 -0.4911, ve-822 -0.4233, olaparib -1.0163, talazoparib -2.0653) lives in fet-ddr-axis-scan.json -> atr_inhibitor_sensitivity_gdsc.by_drug.*.welch_line_median_corrected. Every one reproduces exactly - the artifacts are right, the provenance sentence names the wrong one. Correct only under the reading 'every number in parts A-D'.
p1s.fix: Scope it: 'Every number in parts A-D is produced by emc_atr_vulnerability.py...; the structural numbers in the headline come from emc_fet_idr_census.py / emc_fet_construct_designs.py and the imported group difference from fet_ddr_axis_scan.py, each with its own --check.'

p1s.summary: S2.1's superseded expression reading was corrected in the prose and not in the producing module or its artifact, so the artifact a reader is sent to still carries the withdrawn interpretation.
p1s.evidence: S2.1 now reads 'This row corroborates nothing in either direction', with '(Superseded, retained: "...would be expected to read far higher. Weak corroboration only".)'. research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_a_hemcss_identity.depmap_expression._reading still states 'a floor-level NR4A3 is evidence against the label', and evidence_chain[1] still ends '...would be expected to read far higher in absolute terms. Reported as weak corroboration only.' The prose is correct now; nothing keeps the pair aligned, and S7 tells the reader the artifact is the home of every statement.
p1s.fix: Propagate the correction into emc_atr_vulnerability.py's _reading and evidence_chain strings and regenerate, or carry S8.3's index-confound sentence there so both copies say the same thing.

what_i_read: git log -S at the pin over research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py and research/modalities/depmap_sarcoma_dependency.py

p2s.summary: The standard error quoted in S5 is the expression rows' n, not the passing row's.
p2s.evidence: S5: 'At n ~ 700 the standard error on a single rho is ~ 0.038 ... +0.2123 clears it by 0.0155, 0.41x that standard error.' In emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity['dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1_mean_gene_effect'].per_drug_rho_ATR_inhibitors the n is 597 (azd6738) and 565 (ve-822), not 704/711, so that row's SE is ~0.041 and the margin is ~0.38x SE. The reading is unchanged, and the paper already flags that the two scores come from different line sets.

p2s.summary: S4 calls the pooled-panel SD a within-group SD, and the number collides with the ATM row printed above it.
p2s.evidence: S4: 'a FET-minus-matched delta of -0.0065 against a within-group SD of 0.190'. The artifact value is part_c_coordinated_dependency.knockout_instrument_with_matched_comparator.axis_sd_sarcoma_pool = 0.1904, the SD of the axis across the pooled sarcoma panel (FET + comparator), not within either group - and it is numerically indistinguishable from the ATM row's panel_sd 0.1901 four lines above.

p2s.summary: A word is added inside quotation marks presented as the source's own bound.
p2s.evidence: Headline: 'what that re-cut supports is "FET-rearranged lines are broadly drug-sensitive, including but not especially to ATR inhibitors" - verbatim the bound its own source places on it'. research/manuscripts/program/emc-post-degrader-options.md lines 411-413 read: 'this dataset supports "FET-rearranged lines are drug-sensitive, including but not especially to ATR inhibitors"; it does **not** isolate ATR, and it must not be written as if it did.' The italic clause marked verbatim IS verbatim; the bolded quotation before it inserts 'broadly'. The insertion strengthens the caveat rather than weakening it, but it sits inside quote marks.

p2s.summary: The producing module and its artifact cite Bangerter as Hum Cell 2022 where the manuscript says 2023.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript S2.2 and the Appendix both read 'Hum Cell 2023;36:446-455'. research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py line ~2366 and research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature._limits both read 'Bangerter et al. (Hum Cell 2022; PMID 36316541)'. research/literature/submission-reference-metadata-2026-08-09.json and part_a.literature both record 2023, so the manuscript is the correct copy and the module is the stale half of the pair.

p2s.summary: S3.4's closing concordance sentence is the strongest statement in the section and is placed after the power caveat that qualifies it.
p2s.evidence: S3.4 reads 'Part B's nulls are at n = 10 and n = 6 EMC tumours and no minimum detectable effect was computed, so their agreement is consistency between two underpowered reads, not a demonstration that a DDR signal is absent', then four paragraphs later 'That concordance is what makes this a result rather than a single series' quirk.' Both are defensible together - one is about series-specific artefacts, the other about power - but the stronger one is last and bolded, and the headline imports it without the power caveat travelling with it.

objections_i_raised_and_the_paper_alread: That the paper bounds its negative on more sides than its instruments allow - the strongest available objection on this lens. S6.1's final paragraph pre-empts it in terms: 'the bound is on ONE side, not three - this paragraph used to claim three, and two of them were instruments this document declares incapable', naming part C as a failure to look (quoting S4's own prohibition, 'it must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis... It cannot refute it') and part D's ATM row as a bound on the proxy only. I found no surviving passage that counts either as a null.

That 'the RGG dose-calibration prediction - EMC placed on the FET/ATR authors' own published RGG calibration curve' is a type-2-only claim dressed as an EMC claim, one row below the table that makes the type-1/type-2 distinction the point. Refuted against emc-fet-construct-designs.json -> rgg_dose_calibration_and_predictions.emc_constructs_on_the_same_axis, which places all four constructs (type 1 0.267, type 2 0.0, type 5 0.367, TAF15 0.0); registered_predictions P2 is explicitly about type 1 as 'the COMMONEST EMC fusion' and P4 about the type-1/type-2 pair as a naturally occurring dose series.

That 'fixed before the numbers' is unfalsifiable, or that a cut moved once the numbers were visible. Refuted: git log -S at the pin returns exactly one commit for each quoted cut - the '> 0.2' elevation comparison, 'bool(ddr_up_adj) and len(ctrl_up) <= 1', 'abs(a) > 0.1 and abs(a) > 1.5 * abs(c0)', 'abs(rho) > abs(prolif_rho) * 1.15' and 'n_pass >= 2' in emc_atr_vulnerability.py, and 'DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD = -0.5' in depmap_sarcoma_dependency.py - i.e. the commit that introduced it, never changed since. All are also quoted verbatim and correctly in S1.

That the Appendix claims the uncited '~5-11 % of EMC carries no identified FET partner' was removed from the producing module when it was not. Refuted: emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 2359-2366 carry only a comment recording the removal and the sourced Bangerter bound in its place; the figure is absent from module and artifact.

That the Bangerter '> 90 %' quotation is typed from recollection. Refuted: the full abstract is committed verbatim in research/manuscripts/aso/lit-targets-aso-verify.json, and the same sentence in hemcss-label-priorart.json -> the_counterweight.

That the one passing mechanism test is quoted as evidence for ATR. Refuted at length in S5 - 'an internal-consistency check passing, at MODULE level rather than at target level', MK-1775 at +0.157 beside berzosertib's +0.173 with no interval computed, and 'no bar in this analysis separates ATR from a neighbouring checkpoint kinase'.

That the 'vs non-DDR drugs' column is presented as a specificity control. Refuted: S5 discloses it is a signed mean over two opposite-sign drugs, that it records cancellation on every expression row, and that the paper's own plain-proliferation control passes it - and files rather than applies the |rho| re-grading, which is the anti-gaming rule.

That the WEAK tier is asserted where neither series instantiates the verbatim criterion. The paper says so itself in S6.1 ('Neither series instantiates the verbatim WEAK criterion... and this paragraph used to say both did').

That the headline's imported group-difference numbers are selected. All six reproduce exactly against fet-ddr-axis-scan.json welch_line_median_corrected, and the two drugs that would flatter the hypothesis (mk-1775 +0.0212, bortezomib +0.0869) are the two it does not need and does not hide.
notes: I re-derived every printed statistic in parts A-D, S3.4 and S8.3 from the committed artifacts at the pin and they reproduce: part C's per-gene table and coordination block, part D's four-predictor table, its seven-drug family table and both the signed and |rho| control means, part B's GSE4303 and GSE24369 contrasts and probe-mapping diagnostics, part A's Cellosaurus ST block (16 distinct markers over 18 lines) and DepMap readouts, and S8.3's TPM and family-fraction ranks. The arithmetic is clean and the fixed cuts are genuinely fixed. What my lens found instead is three statements about SOURCES rather than numbers, each contradicted by a committed artifact - what PMID 34413129 says about this line (the largest, and fixing it strengthens S2 rather than weakening it), how far apart the two part-B series are, and whether the Cancer Letters abstract was ever read - plus one tumour-entity mislabel inherited from a substring-matching classifier. The structural objection my lens exists to press, that the negative is bounded on more sides than the instruments can bound, is already answered explicitly and in the right place. Referee verdict: MINOR REVISION - none of the four blockers changes a verdict, a tier or a number, and all four are one-to-three-sentence corrections against artifacts already in the repository. Disclosure: while grepping the repository at the pin for the string 'harbor in > 90' I inadvertently surfaced one line of research/autonomy/hardening-state/PUB-ATR.json in grep output. I did not open that file and no finding above derives from it; the citation-year point it mentioned I then checked directly against the manuscript, where both copies already read 2023, so it is not filed.
